text.p: The following stories were reported in Lithuanian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government plans to recall seven ambassadors in the cabinet meeting today. It is expected that the ambassadors in Finland, France, Belarus, Estonia and Sweden may have their tour of duty ended.
- After an increase of excise taxes, prices for alcohol and fuel rose on Tuesday. A litre of diesel fuel ranged between 1.35-1.36 litas and A95 petroleum costed 1.8-1.95 litas.
- Central bank chief Reinoldijus Sharkinas reassured the representatives of the World Bank on Tuesday that the exchange rate of the litas and the dollar will not change this year or next year.
- Austrian Creditantstalt Investment Bank will next week send its experts group to research Lithuania's financial market next week.
- Klaipedos Nafta will hold talks with Russia's Jukos oil concern over an increase of oil exports via the terminal this week.
- Parliament's national security and foreign affairs comittee said on Tuesday said that the country was aiming to be accepted into NATO during the first stage of expansion.
- Oil extraction in Lithuania doubled in the first quarter of 1997 to 56,000 tonnes compared to 28,000 tonnes.
- The reconstruction of Klaipeda Nafta oil terminal worth $120 million should be over in the first quarter of 1998.
- German Chancellor Helmut Kohl confirmed Germany's support to Lithuania's democratic reforms and its integration to EU and NATO during a meeting with parliament chairman Vytautas Landsbergis.
- Lithuanian Telecom plans to acquire some 1.2 percent of Lintel telephone exchange to boost its stake to 51 percent in the company. U.S. West has 49 percent.
- The turnover of Lithuania's lottery market in 1996 was 85.6 million litas.
- LUKoil Baltija reported 66.1 million litas profit in 1996 versu 14.1 million litas a year before.
